newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Parvanov set to become Bulgarian premier.
newsitem.headline: Parvanov set to become Bulgarian premier.

text.p: Bulgaria's ruling Socialist Party on Tuesday elected Georgi Parvanov as its leader and prime minister-designate to replace Zhan Videnov who resigned at the weekend.
Parvanov's appointment as prime minister must be approved by parliament where the Socialists have a majority.
"This is a sign of the commitment of the Socialist Party to reform," Parvanov told the party's congress after his election.
A showdown between hardliners and reformists in the party entered its final phase on Monday as congress delegates prepared to vote for a new leader and prime minister.

After Prime Minister Videnov's surprise resignation on Saturday, Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev led the attack with an outspoken condemnation of the government's failure to halt economic collapse and fight corruption.
But Videnov's supporters fought back, ensuring he was presented again as a candidate for the leadership.
Bulgaria's lev currency has fallen steadily since the beginning of the year and sharply in the past two months as Bulgarians withdrew their savings from illiquid banks to convert them to dollars.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank have suspended funding over Bulgaria's failure to meet reform targets, including closing or restructuring loss-making state enterprises and privatising viable firms.
The government is preparing the introduction of a currency board fixed exchange rate regime proposed by the IMF as a last resort to rescue the economy.

Leading members of the Bulgarian Communist Party renamed themselves Socialists after the end of one-party rule in 1989. The row between hardliners and reformists centred on how far down the road to social democracy they should go.
